title: The creation of the heaven and the earth
summary: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth, and in six days made all that is in them. He saw every thing that He had made, and, behold, it was very good.

title: Adam and Eve in the garden
summary: The LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and put him into the garden to dress it and to keep it.

title: The fall, and the first promise
summary: The serpent beguiled the woman, and they ate. God cursed the serpent and promised the seed that should bruise his head, and drove the man out of Eden.

title: Cain slays Abel
summary: The LORD had respect unto Abel's offering but not unto Cain's; and Cain rose up against his brother in the field and slew him.

title: Enoch walked with God, and was not
summary: Enoch walked with God three hundred years; and he was not, for God took him. He is one of two men Scripture says never saw death.

title: Seth's line reaches Noah
summary: The genealogy records Seth, Enoch, Methuselah and Lamech in the line from Adam to Noah, whom Lamech named in hope of comfort from the work and toil of the ground.

title: The flood
summary: All the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and every living substance was destroyed. Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.

title: God's covenant with Noah
summary: God set His bow in the cloud for a token of the covenant, that the waters should no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.

title: The tower of Babel
summary: Men said, Let us build us a city and a tower whose top may reach unto heaven. The LORD confounded their language and scattered them abroad.

title: The call of Abram
summary: The LORD said, Get thee out of thy country unto a land that I will shew thee, and I will make of thee a great nation. Abram departed, being seventy and five years old.

title: Abram and Lot part company
summary: Their substance was too great to dwell together, so Lot chose all the plain of Jordan and pitched his tent toward Sodom.

title: Melchizedek blesses Abram
summary: The king of Salem, priest of the most high God, brought forth bread and wine and blessed Abram; and Abram gave him tithes of all.

title: Abram believed God
summary: God brought him forth and said, So shall thy seed be. And he believed in the LORD; and He counted it to him for righteousness.

title: Hagar bears Ishmael
summary: Sarai gave her handmaid to Abram, and Hagar bare Ishmael. In the wilderness she called Him Thou God seest me.

title: The covenant of circumcision
summary: God changed Abram's name to Abraham, promised him a son by Sarah, and gave circumcision as the token of an everlasting covenant.

title: Sodom and Gomorrah overthrown
summary: The LORD rained brimstone and fire out of heaven upon the cities of the plain. Lot was brought out, but his wife looked back and became a pillar of salt.

title: The birth of Isaac
summary: The LORD visited Sarah as He had said, and she bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken.

title: Abraham offers Isaac
summary: God said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac. Abraham bound him on the altar, and the angel stayed his hand; a ram was caught in a thicket instead.

title: Sarah buried in the cave of Machpelah
summary: Abraham bought the field and the cave of Ephron the Hittite for a buryingplace, the first ground he held in the land of promise.

title: A wife found for Isaac
summary: Abraham's servant prayed at the well, and Rebekah came out with her pitcher and gave his camels drink. She went with him, and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.

title: Jacob and Esau born
summary: Rebekah was barren until Isaac entreated the LORD. Two nations were in her womb, and the elder was told he should serve the younger.

title: Esau sells his birthright
summary: Esau came in faint from the field and sold his birthright to Jacob for bread and pottage of lentiles; thus Esau despised his birthright.

title: Jacob takes the blessing
summary: At Rebekah's counsel Jacob came to his blind father in Esau's raiment and received the blessing; and Esau hated him for it.

title: Jacob's ladder at Bethel
summary: Fleeing from Esau, Jacob dreamed of a ladder set up on the earth reaching to heaven, and the LORD renewed to him the promise made to Abraham.

title: Jacob serves twenty years for Laban
summary: He served seven years for Rachel and they seemed but a few days for the love he had to her; Laban gave him Leah first, and changed his wages ten times.

title: Jacob wrestles at Peniel
summary: A man wrestled with him until the breaking of the day. Jacob would not let Him go except He blessed him, and his name was changed to Israel.

title: Jacob and Esau meet again
summary: Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept.

title: Rachel dies bearing Benjamin
summary: Rachel had hard labour in the way to Ephrath, and died; and Jacob set a pillar upon her grave.

title: Dinah at Shechem
summary: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went out to see the daughters of the land at Shechem, where Shechem the Hivite took her and defiled her.

title: Judah and Tamar
summary: Judah acknowledged Tamar's righteousness after she conceived Pharez and Zarah, preserving the family line recorded in Genesis.

title: Joseph sold into Egypt
summary: His brethren hated him for his dreams and his coat, cast him into a pit, and sold him to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver.

title: Joseph in Potiphar's house and in prison
summary: The LORD was with Joseph and he was a prosperous man; falsely accused, he was put into the prison, and the LORD was with him there also.

title: Joseph raised over all Egypt
summary: Joseph read Pharaoh's dream of seven plenteous and seven lean years, and Pharaoh set him over all the land of Egypt.

title: Joseph makes himself known to his brethren
summary: He said, I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt; be not grieved, for God did send me before you to preserve life.

title: Israel goes down into Egypt
summary: Jacob took all he had and came into Egypt, threescore and ten souls, and they dwelt in the land of Goshen and grew there.

title: Jacob blesses his twelve sons
summary: Dying, he told them what should befall them in the last days, and said the sceptre should not depart from Judah until Shiloh come.

title: The death of Joseph
summary: Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old, having made the children of Israel swear to carry up his bones out of Egypt.

title: The trial and restoring of Job
summary: Job lost his goods, his children and his health in one day, yet sinned not with his lips; and the LORD turned his captivity and gave him twice as much as he had before.

title: Israel in bondage in Egypt
summary: A new king arose who knew not Joseph, and set taskmasters over Israel to afflict them with burdens, and made their lives bitter with hard bondage.

title: The birth of Moses
summary: Hidden three months and then laid in an ark of bulrushes, he was drawn out of the water by Pharaoh's daughter and nursed by his own mother.

title: Moses flees to Midian
summary: Having slain an Egyptian, he fled from Pharaoh and dwelt in the land of Midian, where he married Zipporah and kept the flock of Jethro.

title: The burning bush
summary: The bush burned with fire and was not consumed. God called him to bring Israel out of Egypt, and named Himself I AM THAT I AM.

title: The ten plagues upon Egypt
summary: Blood, frogs, lice, flies, murrain, boils, hail, locusts, darkness, and the death of the firstborn; and the LORD put a division between Egypt and His people.

title: The passover
summary: The lamb was killed and its blood struck on the door posts: When I see the blood, I will pass over you. At midnight the firstborn of Egypt died.

title: Israel goes out of Egypt
summary: At the end of four hundred and thirty years all the hosts of the LORD went out, led by a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.

title: The Red sea divided
summary: The LORD caused the sea to go back and the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon dry ground; the waters returned upon the Egyptians.

title: The bitter waters made sweet
summary: At Marah the water was bitter; the LORD shewed Moses a tree, and he cast it into the waters and they were made sweet. Then they came to Elim.

title: Manna in the wilderness
summary: There lay a small round thing upon the ground, and they said, It is manna. Israel did eat manna forty years, until they came to a land inhabited.

title: Water out of the rock
summary: There was no water for the people to drink, and the LORD stood upon the rock in Horeb; Moses smote it, and water came out.

title: Amalek defeated at Rephidim
summary: While Moses held up his hand Israel prevailed; Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands until the going down of the sun, and Joshua discomfited Amalek.

title: Jethro's counsel
summary: Seeing Moses judge the people alone from morning to evening, Jethro told him to place able men, such as fear God, as rulers over thousands and hundreds.

title: The law given at Sinai
summary: The LORD came down upon the mount in fire and spake the ten commandments, and gave Moses two tables of stone written with the finger of God.

title: The golden calf
summary: While Moses was in the mount the people made a molten calf; he came down, and his anger waxed hot, and he brake the tables beneath the mount.

title: The tabernacle set up
summary: On the first day of the first month the tabernacle was reared up, and a cloud covered it, and the glory of the LORD filled it.

title: Strange fire before the LORD
summary: Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire which He commanded them not, and there went out fire from the LORD and devoured them.

title: The day of atonement appointed
summary: Once a year the high priest went within the veil with blood, and the scapegoat bore away the iniquities of the people unto a land not inhabited.

title: The twelve spies, and Israel's refusal
summary: Ten brought an evil report; Caleb said, Let us go up at once and possess it. The people would not, and were turned back into the wilderness.

title: Forty years in the wilderness
summary: A year for each day the spies searched the land, until all that generation fell in the wilderness; their clothes waxed not old upon them.

title: Korah's rebellion
summary: Korah, Dathan and Abiram gathered against Moses and Aaron; the earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up, and they went down alive into the pit.

title: The brasen serpent
summary: Fiery serpents bit the people; Moses made a serpent of brass and set it on a pole, and every one that beheld it lived.

title: Balaam hired to curse Israel
summary: The ass spake with man's voice and turned Balaam back; three times he was hired to curse, and three times he blessed, and foretold a Star out of Jacob.

title: Phinehas turns away the plague
summary: When Israel joined itself to Baalpeor, Phinehas rose up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; he was given a covenant of an everlasting priesthood.

title: Moses dies on Mount Nebo
summary: The LORD shewed him all the land from the top of Pisgah, and he died there; his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated, and no man knows his grave.

title: Joshua commissioned
summary: Arise, go over this Jordan. Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.

title: Rahab hides the spies
summary: She hid them with the stalks of flax on the roof, and bound the scarlet line in her window, and she and all her father's house were saved.

title: Israel crosses Jordan on dry ground
summary: The priests bearing the ark stood firm in the midst of Jordan while all Israel passed over, and twelve stones were set up for a memorial.

title: The walls of Jericho fall
summary: They compassed the city once a day for six days and seven times on the seventh; the people shouted, and the wall fell down flat.

title: Achan's sin, and the taking of Ai
summary: Israel fled before Ai because of the accursed thing hidden in Achan's tent; when it was put away, the LORD gave the city into their hand.

title: The law read at Ebal and Gerizim
summary: Joshua built an altar of whole stones, wrote upon them a copy of the law of Moses, and read all the blessings and cursings before all Israel.

title: The sun stands still at Gibeon
summary: The sun stood still and the moon stayed until the people had avenged themselves; there was no day like that before it or after it.

title: Hazor and the northern kings taken
summary: Joshua turned back and took Hazor, the head of all those kingdoms, and burnt it with fire.

title: The land divided by lot
summary: The tabernacle was set up at Shiloh, and Eleazar and Joshua divided the inheritance among the tribes; Caleb asked for Hebron and received it.

title: Choose you this day
summary: Joshua gathered the tribes to Shechem and said, As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD; and the people answered that they would serve Him also.

title: Othniel, the first judge
summary: When Israel cried unto the LORD He raised up a deliverer; the Spirit of the LORD came upon Othniel, and the land had rest forty years.

title: Ehud delivers Israel from Moab
summary: A man lefthanded, he brought a present to Eglon king of Moab and slew him with a dagger; and the land had rest fourscore years.

title: Ruth gleans in the field of Boaz
summary: Ruth clave to Naomi and came back with her to Bethlehem; her hap was to light on the field of Boaz, who redeemed her, and she bare Obed, grandfather of David.

title: Deborah and Barak against Sisera
summary: Deborah sent Barak with ten thousand men, and the LORD discomfited Sisera's chariots; Jael smote him in her tent, and they sang the song of victory.

title: Gideon's three hundred
summary: The LORD cut the army down to three hundred that Israel might not vaunt itself; with trumpets, pitchers and lamps they routed the host of Midian.

title: Abimelech made king at Shechem
summary: Gideon's son slew his brethren and was made king; Jotham cried his parable from Gerizim, and a woman's millstone ended Abimelech's reign.

title: Jephthah's vow
summary: He vowed that whatsoever came forth of his doors to meet him should be the LORD's; and his daughter came out with timbrels and with dances.

title: Samuel called at Shiloh
summary: The word of the LORD was precious in those days; the child answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth, and the LORD let none of his words fall to the ground.

title: The ark taken, and Ichabod
summary: The Philistines took the ark and slew Hophni and Phinehas; Eli fell backward and died, and the glory was said to be departed from Israel. Dagon fell before the ark at Ashdod.

title: Samson betrayed and bound
summary: Delilah pressed him daily till he told her all his heart; his hair was shaven, the LORD departed from him, and the Philistines put out his eyes.

title: Samson's last act
summary: He prayed, O Lord GOD, remember me, and bowed himself with all his might; the house fell upon the lords, and the dead he slew at his death were more than in his life.

title: Israel asks for a king
summary: They said, Make us a king to judge us like all the nations. The LORD told Samuel, They have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me.

title: Saul anointed the first king
summary: Samuel poured the vial of oil upon his head; and when he was presented at Mizpeh the people shouted, God save the king.

title: Saul rejected from being king
summary: To obey is better than sacrifice. Because he had rejected the word of the LORD, the LORD rejected him from being king over Israel.

title: David anointed at Bethlehem
summary: The LORD seeth not as man seeth; man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart. Samuel anointed the youngest son of Jesse.

title: David and Goliath
summary: Thou comest to me with a sword, but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts. David prevailed with a sling and a stone.

title: Saul hunts David
summary: Saul eyed David from the day of the women's song, and sought him in the wilderness; Jonathan loved him, and Michal let him down through a window.

title: David and Abigail
summary: Abigail met David with provisions and wise words, and David blessed the LORD for sending her to keep him from avenging himself with his own hand.

title: David spares the LORD's anointed
summary: Twice David had Saul in his hand, in the cave and in the trench, and twice he would not stretch forth his hand against the LORD's anointed.

title: Saul and the woman of Endor
summary: The LORD answered him not, neither by dreams nor by prophets, so on the eve of battle he sought out a woman that had a familiar spirit.

title: Saul and Jonathan fall at Gilboa
summary: The battle went sore against Saul, and he fell upon his own sword. David lamented over him and Jonathan: How are the mighty fallen.

title: David made king over all Israel
summary: After reigning seven years and six months in Hebron over Judah, all the elders came to him and anointed him king over Israel; he reigned forty years in all.

title: David honors Mephibosheth
summary: David sought out Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, and restored Saul's fields to him, setting him continually at the king's table for Jonathan's sake.

title: David takes the stronghold of Zion
summary: He took the strong hold of Zion from the Jebusites, and dwelt in the fort, and called it the city of David.

title: The ark brought up to Jerusalem
summary: David danced before the LORD with all his might, and brought up the ark with shouting and the sound of the trumpet; Michal despised him in her heart.

title: God's covenant with David
summary: By Nathan the LORD promised to set up his seed after him: thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee.

title: David's sin, and his repentance
summary: He took the wife of Uriah and set her husband in the forefront of the battle. Nathan said, Thou art the man; and David said, I have sinned against the LORD.

title: Absalom's rebellion
summary: Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel and drove his father out of Jerusalem; he was caught by his head in an oak, and Joab slew him.

title: Solomon made king
summary: Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him at Gihon, and the throne of David his father was established greatly.

title: Solomon asks for an understanding heart
summary: God appeared to him in a dream at Gibeon and said, Ask what I shall give thee; and because he asked for wisdom, riches and honour were added.

title: Solomon builds the house of the LORD
summary: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the exodus he began to build; when it was finished the cloud filled the house, so that the priests could not stand to minister.

title: The queen of Sheba comes to Jerusalem
summary: She came to prove him with hard questions, and when she had seen his wisdom there was no more spirit in her; the half had not been told her.

title: Solomon's heart turned away
summary: His wives turned away his heart after other gods when he was old, and the LORD said He would rend the kingdom from his son, leaving one tribe for David's sake.

title: The kingdom divided
summary: Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the old men and answered roughly; ten tribes said, What portion have we in David? and made Jeroboam king.

title: The golden calves at Bethel and Dan
summary: Lest the people go up to Jerusalem, Jeroboam made two calves of gold and said, Behold thy gods, O Israel; and this thing became a sin.

title: Elijah and the three years' drought
summary: He said there should be neither dew nor rain but according to his word; he was fed by ravens, then by a widow whose barrel of meal did not waste.

title: The widow's son raised at Zarephath
summary: Elijah stretched himself upon the child three times and cried unto the LORD, and the soul of the child came into him again.

title: The fire falls on Carmel
summary: How long halt ye between two opinions? The fire of the LORD fell and consumed the sacrifice, the wood, the stones and the water, and the people fell on their faces.

title: The still small voice at Horeb
summary: The LORD was not in the wind, nor the earthquake, nor the fire, but in a still small voice; and He told Elijah of seven thousand who had not bowed to Baal.

title: Naboth's vineyard
summary: Jezebel had Naboth stoned on false witness so Ahab could take his vineyard, and Elijah met the king with the word of judgment.

title: Elijah taken up by a whirlwind
summary: A chariot of fire and horses of fire parted them asunder, and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven; Elisha took up his mantle.

title: Naaman washes in Jordan
summary: He was wroth at so small a word, but dipped seven times as the prophet said, and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child.

title: Jehu destroys the house of Ahab
summary: Anointed to cut off Ahab's house, he threw Jezebel down from the window and destroyed Baal out of Israel, yet kept the calves of Jeroboam.

title: Joash hidden, and crowned at seven
summary: Athaliah destroyed the seed royal, but the babe was hid in the house of the LORD six years; then they crowned him and clapped their hands.

title: Jonah sent to Nineveh
summary: He fled toward Tarshish and was three days and three nights in the fish's belly; then he preached, and the people of Nineveh believed God.

title: Isaiah sees the Lord
summary: He saw the Lord high and lifted up, and his lips were touched with a live coal; and he answered, Here am I; send me.

title: Israel carried away to Assyria
summary: The king of Assyria took Samaria and carried Israel away, because they had not obeyed the voice of the LORD their God.

title: Fifteen years added to Hezekiah
summary: Sick unto death, he turned his face to the wall and wept; the LORD heard his prayer, healed him, and turned the shadow back on the sundial.

title: Sennacherib turned back from Jerusalem
summary: Hezekiah spread the letter before the LORD, and the angel of the LORD smote the camp of the Assyrians; and Sennacherib returned to Nineveh.

title: Manasseh's long evil reign, and his repentance
summary: He filled Jerusalem with innocent blood; taken with hooks to Babylon, he humbled himself greatly, and then he knew that the LORD He was God.

title: Jeremiah called to be a prophet
summary: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee. The LORD touched his mouth and set him over the nations, to root out and to plant.

title: The book of the law found
summary: Hilkiah found the book in the house of the LORD; Josiah rent his clothes, enquired of Huldah, and made a covenant to walk after the LORD with all his heart.

title: The king cuts and burns the roll
summary: Jehoiakim cut the roll with a penknife and cast it into the fire; Jeremiah dictated it again to Baruch, and many like words were added.

title: Jeremiah cast into the dungeon
summary: They let him down with cords into the mire for saying the city would be taken; Ebedmelech the Ethiopian drew him out with old cast clouts and rags.

title: The writing prophets speak
summary: The KJV introduces Hosea, Amos, Micah, Obadiah, Nahum, Habakkuk and Zephaniah as prophets whose books address Israel, Judah, Edom, Nineveh and Babylon.

title: The first captives carried to Babylon
summary: Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem and carried away part of the vessels of the house of God, and certain of the king's seed, among them Daniel.

title: The image of gold, silver, brass and iron
summary: Daniel told the king both the dream and its meaning: four kingdoms, and then a kingdom set up by the God of heaven which shall never be destroyed.

title: Ezekiel among the captives by Chebar
summary: The heavens were opened and he saw visions of God; the LORD sent him to a rebellious nation and made him a watchman unto the house of Israel.

title: Jerusalem and the temple burnt
summary: The house of the LORD, the king's house and all the houses of Jerusalem were burnt with fire, and the walls broken down round about.

title: The valley of dry bones
summary: O ye dry bones, hear the word of the LORD. The breath came into them and they lived, a sign that God would open the graves of His people and bring them into their own land.

title: The burning fiery furnace
summary: The three would not bow to the image; cast into the furnace heated seven times, they walked loose with a fourth like the Son of God, and the fire had no power over them.

title: Nebuchadnezzar driven from men
summary: He boasted of great Babylon that he had built, and was driven to eat grass as oxen until he knew that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men.

title: The writing on the wall
summary: As they drank from the vessels of God's house, fingers of a man's hand wrote MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN; that night Belshazzar was slain.

title: The seventy weeks
summary: Reading in Jeremiah of the seventy years, Daniel prayed and confessed; Gabriel came and told him of seventy weeks determined upon his people and upon the holy city.

title: Daniel in the lions' den
summary: He kneeled three times a day toward Jerusalem as he did aforetime; cast to the lions, he was kept, for God had sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths.

title: The decree of Cyrus
summary: The LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, who proclaimed that the house of the LORD in Jerusalem should be built, and let the people go up.

title: The foundation of the second house laid
summary: The people shouted with a great shout, but the old men who had seen the first house wept with a loud voice, so that the noise could not be discerned.

title: Haggai and Zechariah stir up the building
summary: Is it time for you to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste? Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.

title: The second temple finished
summary: The house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, and the children of Israel kept the dedication of this house of God with joy.

title: Esther made queen of Persia
summary: The king loved Esther above all the women, and set the royal crown upon her head; she had not shewed her people nor her kindred.

title: Haman's plot overthrown
summary: Esther went in unto the king unbidden, saying, If I perish, I perish. Haman was hanged on his own gallows, and the Jews had light and gladness.

title: Ezra brings the law to Jerusalem
summary: He had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD and to do it and to teach it; the Levites read distinctly and gave the sense, and caused the people to understand.

title: Nehemiah rebuilds the wall
summary: Come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we be no more a reproach. It was finished in fifty and two days, with a weapon in every hand.

title: The last word before the silence
summary: Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me; and I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and dreadful day of the LORD.

title: The kingdoms of the silent years foretold
summary: Scripture itself is what tells of these years: Daniel was shewn the ram and the he goat, named as Media and Persia and Grecia, and the kings that should stand up after.

title: Four hundred years of silence
summary: After Malachi's promise of the messenger, Scripture records no prophet until the days of Herod, when the angel Gabriel stood by the altar of incense.

title: Gabriel promises a son to Zacharias
summary: As he burned incense the angel said, Thy prayer is heard, and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.

title: The annunciation to Mary
summary: Thou shalt conceive, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS. And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.

title: The birth of John the Baptist
summary: His father wrote, His name is John, and his mouth was opened immediately; and he prophesied of the dayspring from on high.

title: The birth of Jesus Christ
summary: She brought forth her firstborn son and laid him in a manger, for there was no room in the inn; and the angel said, Unto you is born this day a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.

title: Presented in the temple
summary: Simeon took him up in his arms and blessed God, having been promised he should not see death first; and Anna spake of him to all that looked for redemption.

title: The wise men, and the flight into Egypt
summary: They opened their treasures and presented gold, frankincense and myrrh; warned in a dream, Joseph fled into Egypt, and Herod slew the children of Bethlehem.

title: About my Father's business
summary: At twelve years old he was found in the temple among the doctors, hearing them and asking questions; and all that heard him were astonished at his understanding.

title: The baptism of Jesus
summary: John said, Behold the Lamb of God. The heavens were opened, the Spirit descended like a dove, and a voice said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

title: The temptation in the wilderness
summary: Forty days fasting, He answered every temptation with It is written, and said, Get thee hence, Satan; then the devil left him and angels came and ministered.

title: Water turned to wine at Cana
summary: This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; and his disciples believed on him.

title: Ye must be born again
summary: A ruler of the Jews came by night, and was told that except a man be born again he cannot see the kingdom of God. For God so loved the world.

title: The woman at the well
summary: Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst. Many of the Samaritans believed, and said, This is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world.

title: Philip finds Nathanael
summary: Philip found Nathanael and told him of Jesus of Nazareth; Nathanael came and confessed, Rabbi, thou art the Son of God, thou art the King of Israel.

title: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men
summary: By the sea He called Simon and Andrew, and James and John mending their nets; and they straightway left all and followed him.

title: The sermon on the mount
summary: Blessed are the poor in spirit. He taught the beatitudes, the light of the world, the Lord's prayer and the two foundations; and the people were astonished at his doctrine.

title: The calling of Matthew
summary: He saw a publican at the receipt of custom and said, Follow me; and he arose and followed him, and made him a feast in his house.

title: The twelve apostles chosen
summary: He continued all night in prayer to God, and when it was day he chose twelve, whom he also named apostles, and sent them forth to preach.

title: Peace, be still
summary: He rebuked the wind and said unto the sea, Peace, be still; and there was a great calm, and they feared exceedingly.

title: Five loaves and two fishes
summary: He gave thanks and distributed to them that were set down as much as they would; about five thousand men were filled, and twelve baskets of fragments remained.

title: Walking on the sea
summary: In the fourth watch He went unto them walking on the sea; Peter walked to Him, and beginning to sink cried, Lord, save me, and immediately He caught him.

title: Thou art the Christ
summary: Whom say ye that I am? Peter answered, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; and He said flesh and blood had not revealed it to him.

title: The transfiguration
summary: His face did shine as the sun and his raiment was white as the light; Moses and Elias appeared with him, and a voice out of the cloud said, Hear ye him.

title: Lazarus raised from the dead
summary: I am the resurrection, and the life. Four days in the grave, Lazarus came forth at His cry, bound hand and foot with graveclothes.

title: Zacchaeus comes down
summary: Make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house. The Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.

title: The triumphal entry
summary: The multitudes cried, Hosanna to the Son of David, as He rode into Jerusalem upon an ass, as Zechariah had said the King would come.

title: The last supper
summary: He took bread and brake it, saying, This is my body; and the cup, This is my blood of the new testament. And He gave them a new commandment, to love one another.

title: Gethsemane, and the betrayal
summary: O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, thy will be done. Judas came with a multitude and betrayed Him with a kiss.

title: Before Caiaphas and Pilate
summary: He confessed before the high priest that He was the Christ; Pilate found no fault in Him, washed his hands, released Barabbas and gave sentence.

title: The crucifixion
summary: They crucified Him at the place called Calvary, and two others with Him. He said, It is finished, and gave up the ghost; and the veil of the temple was rent in twain.

title: The burial
summary: Joseph of Arimathaea craved the body and wrapped it in linen, and Nicodemus brought myrrh and aloes; they laid Him in a new tomb wherein was never man yet laid.

title: The resurrection
summary: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord.

title: The road to Emmaus
summary: Beginning at Moses and all the prophets, He expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself; and they knew him in the breaking of bread.

title: My Lord and my God
summary: Reach hither thy finger, and be not faithless, but believing. Thomas answered, My Lord and my God; and Jesus blessed them that have not seen, and yet have believed.

title: The great commission
summary: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost; and, lo, I am with you alway.

title: The ascension
summary: While they beheld, He was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight; and two men in white apparel said He should so come in like manner.

title: Matthias numbered with the eleven
summary: They prayed, Thou, Lord, which knowest the hearts of all men, shew whether of these two thou hast chosen; and the lot fell upon Matthias.

title: The day of Pentecost
summary: There came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and cloven tongues like as of fire sat upon each of them; that day about three thousand souls were added.

title: Silver and gold have I none
summary: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk; the man leaped and praised God, and Peter told the council there is none other name given whereby we must be saved.

title: Ananias and Sapphira
summary: They kept back part of the price and lied to the Holy Ghost; both fell down and gave up the ghost, and great fear came upon all the church.

title: Gamaliel's counsel
summary: If this work be of men, it will come to nought: but if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it; lest haply ye be found even to fight against God.

title: Seven men of honest report chosen
summary: The apostles gave themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word, and set seven over the daily ministration, among them Stephen and Philip.

title: Stephen, the first martyr
summary: He saw the heavens opened and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God; as they stoned him he prayed, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge.

title: Philip and the man of Ethiopia
summary: Beginning at the same scripture in Isaiah, he preached unto him Jesus; and they went down into the water and he baptized him.

title: Saul struck down on the road to Damascus
summary: A light from heaven shined round about him, and a voice said, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? Ananias came, and he received sight and was baptized.

title: Tabitha, arise
summary: Peter put them all forth, kneeled down and prayed, and said, Tabitha, arise; she opened her eyes, and many believed in the Lord at Joppa.

title: The Gentiles receive the Holy Ghost
summary: While Peter yet spake the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word, and the brethren said, Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life.

title: The disciples called Christians at Antioch
summary: Barnabas fetched Saul from Tarsus, and a whole year they taught much people; and the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.

title: Peter delivered out of prison
summary: Prayer was made without ceasing for him; the angel smote him on the side, the chains fell off, and the iron gate opened to them of his own accord.

title: The first missionary journey
summary: The Holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul. They sailed to Cyprus and went through Iconium and Lystra, confirming the souls of the disciples.

title: Paul stoned at Lystra
summary: They drew him out of the city supposing he had been dead; but he rose up and went again into the city, saying that through much tribulation we must enter the kingdom of God.

title: The council at Jerusalem
summary: Through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they. James gave sentence, and the burden of the law was not laid upon the Gentiles.

title: Titus travels with Paul
summary: Paul took Titus with him to Jerusalem, where Titus was a Greek and was not compelled to be circumcised; Paul later called him his partner and fellowhelper.

title: Come over into Macedonia, and help us
summary: A vision appeared to Paul in the night at Troas, and immediately they endeavoured to go, assuredly gathering that the Lord had called them to preach there.

title: Lydia, and the jailor at Philippi
summary: The Lord opened Lydia's heart; and at midnight, when Paul and Silas sang praises, the prison shook and the keeper asked, What must I do to be saved?

title: Thessalonica and Berea
summary: Three sabbath days he reasoned out of the scriptures; the Bereans were more noble, receiving the word with all readiness and searching the scriptures daily.

title: Paul's second letter to Thessalonica
summary: Paul, Silvanus and Timotheus addressed the church of the Thessalonians, teaching steadfastness in the coming of the Lord and signing the letter with Paul's own hand.

title: The Unknown God at Athens
summary: Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you. He told them God now commandeth all men every where to repent, and pointed to the day of judgment.

title: A year and six months at Corinth
summary: Be not afraid, but speak: for I have much people in this city. He continued teaching the word of God among them a year and six months.

title: Apollos taught the way more perfectly
summary: Aquila and Priscilla took him unto them and expounded the way of God more perfectly; and he mightily convinced the Jews that Jesus was Christ.

title: Two years at Ephesus
summary: All they which dwelt in Asia heard the word; the books of curious arts were burned, and the silversmiths raised an uproar crying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.

title: Eutychus taken up alive
summary: He fell from the third loft as Paul preached till midnight; Paul fell on him and embraced him, and said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.

title: Paul taken in the temple
summary: All the city was moved, and they drew him out of the temple; from the stairs he told them he was a Jew brought up at the feet of Gamaliel.

title: Before Felix, Festus and Agrippa
summary: Felix trembled as he reasoned of judgment to come; Paul appealed unto Caesar; and Agrippa said, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.

title: Shipwreck on Melita
summary: They all escaped safe to land as the angel had promised; a viper fastened on Paul's hand and he shook it off into the fire and felt no harm.

title: Two whole years in his own hired house
summary: Paul dwelt at Rome with a soldier that kept him, preaching the kingdom of God and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, no man forbidding him.

title: Paul writes for Onesimus
summary: Paul appealed to Philemon for Onesimus, whom he called his son begotten in his bonds and a brother beloved, and sent greetings to the saints at Colosse.

title: I have finished my course
summary: Writing to Timothy from prison, Paul said he had fought a good fight and kept the faith, and that a crown of righteousness was laid up for him.

title: Luke writes to Theophilus
summary: Luke addressed the most excellent Theophilus, writing an orderly account of the things most surely believed among the saints and of all that Jesus began both to do and teach.

title: Jude urges believers to contend
summary: Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, exhorted believers to contend for the faith once delivered unto the saints.

title: Three men named in 3 John
summary: The short letter of 3 John commends Gaius, rejects Diotrephes' preeminence and gives Demetrius a good report of all men and of the truth itself.

title: The Revelation given on Patmos
summary: John was in the isle called Patmos for the word of God, and in the Spirit on the Lord's day heard a great voice; the book ends, Surely I come quickly. Amen.
